mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over three months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint signal does not produce a statistically significant negative return at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month averages signals a robust demand environment, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 7% for two consecutive months signals a deepening labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate cost pressures, ultimately supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive trend in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over a 12-month window signals sustained demand expansion, which consistently boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the business cycle phase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when GDPC1 shows a sustained upward trend over 12 months.
